title: Component-by-component suitability and implementation assessment

decisions.Keep: Retain an existing component or implementation policy in its stated scope. This can be review tooling, not necessarily a public feature.
decisions.Add: Original recommendation to add this capability. Current implementation status separately records the completed showcase work; production content/service conditions still apply.
decisions.Optional: Original recommendation for a conditional enhancement or alternative. Current status distinguishes integrated code, selectable alternatives, review demonstrations and a Custom fallback. Do not stack alternatives.
decisions.Later: Has a specific possible use, but the required real content, scale, service, ownership, license or compatible version does not exist yet.
decisions.Do not add: No justified role in the agreed current website, or conflicts with readability, identity, interaction or service boundaries. Not a claim of technical impossibility.
decisions.Developer only: Useful implementation/maintenance guidance, with no visitor-facing element to add.
decisions.Reference only: An example, guide, collection or alternative to consult if a specific need arises; not an independent feature selected for implementation.

libraries.conclusion: The interface additions are implemented: Alert/Empty states, AspectRatio media, Field validation and Item document rows, plus conditional utility and reference controls. Marker is correctly used as a section/group label. Radio Group and Native Select are mutually exclusive review alternatives; production forms and document content remain conditional. The future pass also demonstrates Kbd, Checkbox, Toggle, Progress, Table and Pagination in the local source-project checklist.
libraries.avoid: No society login/OTP, chat/AI UI, desktop editor controls or wholesale primitive migration. Keep the current native top-level links.

libraries.conclusion: Shine Border remains the bounded animated accent. BentoGrid and neutral AvatarCircles are integrated optional compositions; static DotPattern/GridPattern are selectable guide backgrounds. Highlighter is represented by a Custom native mark alternative because its extra rough-notation engine was not adopted. The future pass adds a real source-project FileTree, a static literal Terminal and a reader-scoped ScrollProgress demonstration. Code Comparison was inspected and remains deferred because its additional highlighting/theme dependencies were not adopted.
libraries.avoid: No marquee partner wall, fake notifications, invented counters, custom cursor or stacked card-light effects. Recipes inherit their parent decision.

libraries.conclusion: Shared named variants and m + LazyMotion are implemented. The modular build emits a measured separate feature chunk; the portable HTML deliberately embeds it. Bounded orchestration, scope cleanup, visibility hooks and m.create(Card) are review demonstrations with Static/reduced-motion fallbacks; they do not imply live project activity. The future walkthrough now demonstrates scoped reader motion values and useAnimate SVG explanation. Version-gated replacements and paid widgets remain deferred.
libraries.avoid: No drag-only public task, perpetual decorative loop, scroll-speed text or premium page-cover transition. AnimateView is not exported by the pinned version.

libraries.conclusion: Spotlight Card remains restrained. The genuine Folder is now an explicit resource review demonstration with external controls and readable document rows; Static/reduced motion shows a Custom static alternative. Other project/media possibilities remain conditional on real maintained content and exact source/license review. All eleven original Later entries were reassessed; none gains a justified real project/media/data prerequisite from the source walkthrough, so they remain deferred.
libraries.avoid: No new cursor, shader background, moving menu or animated typography in the public shell. Conditional project media needs real content, ownership and source/dependency/license review.

libraries.conclusion: The small named-import semantic set now includes the accepted Clock, TriangleAlert, Handshake, BookOpen, CodeXml, Copy and Link uses alongside existing icons. Text labels retain meaning. Unselected catalogue icons remain unimported; icon availability is not an implementation claim. Six original Later icons now reinforce the local walkthrough: ArrowLeft, GitBranch, Terminal, Workflow, FileCode and ListFilter. Other technical symbols still lack distinct assigned content.
libraries.avoid: Do not use icon volume as decoration, invent account/services from symbols, replace actual brand marks or include React Native guidance in the web build.

method: Every retained catalogue ID has a decision, a current-scope rationale, where/how guidance, a reconsideration condition, an alternative, a technical gate and links to the earlier D-series design decisions.

The assessment order is shadcn/ui → Magic UI → Motion → React Bits → Lucide React. The subsequent implementation pass maps every Add/Optional row in implemented-upgrades.json. Each row now distinguishes integrated code, selectable alternatives, review demonstrations and a Custom static fallback.

Named standard components and selected creative/API cases have explicit judgements. Repeated visual families and the icon long tail use disclosed product policies with entry-specific identity/context; the Review basis field tells you which. This is not a claim of separately visual-testing every icon or executing every creative component.
The 170 Magic UI recipes each map to a named parent component and inherit its content/placement conditions. They remain reference examples, not 170 separate recommendations.

Every canonical icon has a semantic use/no-use decision. Its file availability is checked against pinned lucide-react; the shortlist has explicit meanings. Unselected shapes are not technically forbidden: they have no current assigned meaning.

Paid collections are assessed at the publicly named family level. Unlisted variants and inaccessible licensed source are not claimed to be individually inspected. Source/version/license/dependency review remains a gate before any conditional adoption.

React Native entries accidentally present in the broader catalogue are retained for traceability and explicitly rejected for this React DOM site. Lucide inherited category metadata is resolved before grouping; raw source directives are not treated as user-facing categories.

The installed Motion namespaces were inspected locally. AnimateView is absent from motion/react 14.8.0, so its possible use requires a deliberate compatible upgrade. Export presence does not prove browser behaviour.

Original Add/Optional decisions are retained for traceability. Implementation status and current-use fields record subsequent completed showcase work; Original Later decisions now have a separate futureOutcome: Review demonstration or Still deferred. Current use does not mean approved production content or a connected service.

Implementation status is distinct from the original recommendation and inventory snapshot. The 42 accepted records include overlapping API/topic rows, not 42 independent installed components. Custom fallback does not count as use of its upstream component. Original where/how and if/when describe intended production placement; implementedHow records the actual review example.

D01.title: A task-led public navigation
D01.rationale: Compact society sites make the public tasks legible. Larger umbrella structures demonstrate why HW should avoid exposing a large organisational tree before it has enough active content.

D02.title: A community-led hero with an immediate next step
D02.rationale: Sheffield ties its introduction to an event; Royal Holloway makes membership/chat easy to locate. Edinburgh shows community identity, but finding dates requires a separate route. HW can combine identity with immediate planning.

D03.title: Event cards that answer an attendance decision
D03.rationale: Sheffield supplies practical logistics; Leeds preserves contextual descriptions; Oxford explains beginner preparation; Surrey names venue access features. These address participation barriers better than poster-only listings.

D04.title: One calendar, several ways to subscribe
D04.rationale: Sheffield demonstrates discoverable subscription choices. Oxford shows the risk of maintaining a calendar and image termcard alongside social changes. Edinburgh makes a specialised event platform useful but separate from the main site.

D05.title: A membership page that explains the handoff
D05.rationale: Surrey delegates membership to an institutional product; Illinois distinguishes open participation from paid benefits; Waterloo warns that payment alone does not finish activation. HW should explain its own process rather than copy their fees or rules.

D06.title: Committee cards with a remit, not just a portrait
D06.rationale: Durham and Leeds make jobs understandable. Kent’s year timeline shows continuity but usernames can obscure contact identity. UCLA illustrates why a large roster needs grouping. HW should be clear before becoming elaborate.

D07.title: A readable governance and history shelf
D07.rationale: Edinburgh links its organisational memory; Sheffield and Waterloo publish navigable rules. Surrey’s short aims are useful but should not be confused with a complete operating constitution.

D08.title: A sponsor offer built around achievable outcomes
D08.rationale: Bristol’s formats and enquiry requirements support a decision; Imperial explains channels; UCLA distinguishes support types; Illinois identifies corporate contacts. None establishes HW’s own audience size or commercial terms.

D09.title: Partner recognition that explains the contribution
D09.rationale: Waterloo connects funding to outcomes; UCLA distinguishes institutional support; Edinburgh/CSESoc demonstrate tiered visibility. HW benefits from meaningful attribution without implying every supporter purchased the same package.

D10.title: A small resource library with useful metadata
D10.rationale: Bristol and Oxford provide reusable learning content; CSESoc curates tools with ownership attribution; Waterloo documents resources deeply. HW can earn return visits without operating every tool itself.

D11.title: Inclusion as practical information
D11.rationale: Bristol makes support discoverable, Oxford answers first-visit questions, Surrey supplies venue labels and Leeds describes inclusive activities. The transferable idea is useful detail, not copied institutional advice.

D12.title: A curated first-contribution project shelf
D12.rationale: UCLA Open Source links discovery to beginner tasks. Kent’s project/proposal destinations demonstrate intent but captured loading states do not verify a functioning workflow. Adopt the contribution pattern, not an assumed backend.

D13.title: Interest groups only when there is a real group
D13.rationale: Edinburgh, UCLA and Illinois organise large communities through groups. Oxford advertises focused project groups. Their breadth does not prove HW needs the same structure at launch.

D14.title: Content ownership and expiry built into the design
D14.rationale: Past dates under upcoming headings and older committee/promotion labels show how quickly visual credibility can erode. The design should make freshness a routine publishing property rather than a yearly redesign.

D15.title: Readable, responsive components from the start
D15.rationale: Oxford’s image termcard suggests the need for equivalent text; Sheffield exposes a skip link; horizontally explored histories and very long rosters suggest navigation risks. The research did not conduct a full accessibility audit.

D16.title: An original HW identity with controlled illustrative imagery
D16.rationale: Peer sites demonstrate the value of a coherent identity but do not determine HW’s colours or logo. The asset library, not competitor styling, is the authority for this visual direction.

D17.title: Honest empty, loading and failure states
D17.rationale: Empty event queues do not mean a society is inactive; persistent loading does not prove a functioning feature. A failed sponsor destination illustrates why public email or another approved fallback matters.

D18.title: A deliberate boundary around accounts and services
D18.rationale: The research documents useful services at peers but does not establish HW demand, permissions, infrastructure or capacity. Copying the visible entry point would hide substantial operational work.

reviews.how: Do not import wind-arrow-down as filler. If approved future content genuinely requires the wind arrow down concept, reassess it for that exact label rather than using a vaguely related symbol.
reviews.rationale: The wind arrow down symbol has no distinct assigned action or field in the agreed six pages. Adding it now would duplicate a chosen cue or imply content/service the society has not established.
reviews.condition: Only a real new semantic requirement can reopen this choice; this is a current-scope judgement, not a claim that the SVG cannot render.
reviews.alternative: Plain text; use the small selected icon set only where it improves scanning.
reviews.feasibility: The named icon file exists in pinned lucide-react 1.64.0; this verifies availability, not a visual or screen-reader test of every glyph.
